title: What the stores earned, and who got it
label: The numbers
lede: Toys “R” Us filed annual reports for all twelve of its private years, because its bonds were public. They show a retailer that earned an operating profit in seven of its last eight full years, and a capital structure that took nearly all of it.[^1][^9][^10]

blocks.title: Seventeen years of sales: flat, up, then down
blocks.subtitle: Net sales by fiscal year, $ billions. Numbered points mark the turns.
blocks.xLabel: Fiscal year (ends late January or early February of the following year)

points.title: The Amazon alliance
points.text: Online sales are handed to Amazon under a ten-year agreement.[^32]

points.title: The buyout
points.text: Taken private on July 21, 2005, in a $6.6B merger.[^3]

points.title: The peak
points.text: Net sales of $13.9B in fiscal 2011. The IPO filed in 2010 is still pending.[^10][^11]

points.title: The write-down
points.text: The IPO is withdrawn in March 2013. The year ends with a $1.04B net loss.[^12][^9]

points.title: The last full year
points.text: $11.5B of sales, $460M of operating earnings, $457M of interest.[^1]

blocks.source: Fiscal 2000–2004: 10-K for fiscal 2004, Exhibit 13[^6]. Fiscal 2005–2009: five-year table in the 10-K for fiscal 2009[^7]. Fiscal 2010–2013: statements of operations[^10][^9]. Fiscal 2014–2016: 10-K for fiscal 2016[^1]. Fiscal 2005 is shown as later presented ($11,333M; originally reported as $11,275M[^3]).
